meta.decision_type: Sensory purchase, decided on 'does it smell like the original and will it last'
meta.verdict: Shoppers buy DESIRED because it promises the Wanted by Night experience at a fraction of the price, but the page whispers that promise in small italics and locks the proof (Extrait concentration, 7h longevity, strong projection, night wear) inside an image and a closed accordion. Meanwhile a 15-tier price ticker, a 3-hour countdown that disagrees with the cart's 3-day one, image-based offer cards and two competing buy buttons fight for attention, and the add-to-cart sits below large note photos. The proposal leads with the inspired-by promise and concrete performance facts, shows price per ml on every size, offers 20 ml as a low-risk first try for a non-returnable product, gives one clear button, and keeps every policy intact.

design_plan.direction: Bold nightlife type on a calm retail canvas: the brand's maroon at the edges (bar, header, accents), a neutral decision zone, and one memorable moment: the product name and a 7H · STRONG · NIGHT spec bar in a heavy condensed display face that echoes the brand's uppercase product names.
design_plan.type: Archivo (condensed, 800) for product names and section heads; Hanken Grotesk for body and UI. Mobile scale 12/14/16/20/28/52; desktop 13/15/17/24/30/84. Body 16px on mobile.
design_plan.color: Ink #141212 on white; warm surface #F6F4F1; brand maroon #872824 for tags, savings and links; amber #F6C362 only for 'Best value'; black reserved for the single primary button.
design_plan.layout: Mobile: one column, 16px gutters, 8px rhythm. Desktop: 1200px container, 1.12 : 1 gallery grid and sticky buy box, 56px gap.
design_plan.checks: Single primary CTA; 44px+ touch targets; WCAG AA contrast; one SVG icon family at 1.6 stroke; no emoji icons; tabular figures for prices.

changes.title: One bundle message instead of a 15-tier price ticker
changes.what: The scrolling list of 15 price tiers becomes one line, 'Bundle any scents: 2 × 50 ml at ₹699 each', with arrows to rotate other messages.
changes.why: Nobody reads 15 prices in a moving strip. One clear message about the brand's real AOV lever gets read on every page.

changes.title: Mobile header: menu left, search and bag right
changes.what: Keeps the maroon brand header; drops account and wishlist on mobile, with the heart moving onto the gallery.
changes.why: A familiar, uncluttered header is faster to use; account access isn't needed to buy.

changes.title: Navigation labels without emoji
changes.what: 'OFFERS 🔥' and 'ORIGINALS ✅' become plain labels in one consistent type style.
changes.why: Emoji render differently on every device and read as noise next to an Extrait. One visual language looks more trustworthy.

changes.title: Countdown removed until it matches a real end date
changes.what: Removes 'Sale ends in 02h 59m'. The cart drawer shows a different, 3-day Diwali countdown for the same period.
changes.why: Two timers that disagree read as manufactured urgency. That costs trust, and it is what India's false-urgency rules target.

changes.title: Lead with the inspired-by promise
changes.what: 'Inspired by Wanted by Night' becomes the first thing on the page, as an outlined tag in the brand maroon.
changes.why: This promise is why shoppers clicked. Small italics under the name made them hunt for it.

changes.title: Name plus what it is
changes.what: DESIRED is followed by 'Spiced & fiery woody · Extrait de Parfum · For him', replacing the badges 'Male · Super lasting · Strong projection'.
changes.why: Extrait concentration is real proof of strength; 'super lasting' is a claim every dupe brand makes. The line also says who it's for.

changes.title: Two-line scent description
changes.what: Adds a two-line description from the brand's own meta copy, in its voice.
changes.why: A name alone doesn't tell a shopper what they'll smell. Two lines answer it in the first screen.

changes.title: Rating next to the title
changes.what: A slot for DESIRED's rating and review count. Other scents on the site show ratings; this one shows none.
changes.why: For a blind buy, other buyers' verdict on longevity and likeness is the strongest proof available. Collect it; don't fake it.

changes.title: Price with size and price per ml
changes.what: '50 ml · ₹19.98/ml' sits beside ₹999. The theme's unit-price field renders empty today.
changes.why: Per-ml price makes sizes, and the original, comparable at a glance; India's packaged-commodity rules also expect a unit sale price online.

changes.title: A seven-image gallery plan
changes.what: Two images become a planned set of seven (see the image brief): an arrow and a peek on mobile, a grid on desktop.
changes.why: Scent can't be photographed, so the gallery has to sell the mood, the likeness, the performance, the size and the gift. Two images can't.

changes.title: Longevity, projection and occasion as a spec bar
changes.what: 7H · Strong · Night move out of an infographic image into a bold, readable bar under the gallery.
changes.why: These answer the two biggest dupe doubts: will it last, and will people notice. Before, they were readable only inside the second image.

changes.title: Size tiles with price per ml and a low-risk first try
changes.what: Each size shows its price and per-ml cost; 'Best value' stays on 100 ml. Adds 'New to this scent? Try the 20 ml first, or the tester pack.'
changes.why: Perfumes here are non-returnable, so the fear is a big bottle of a scent you don't like. The 20 ml and the existing tester pack lower that risk at the moment of choice.
changes.impact: Watch AOV and the size mix

changes.title: Bundle and prepaid offers as text
changes.what: Three image offer cards become two text lines: the bundle tiers with 'Build your bundle', and the prepaid code that today appears only in the cart.
changes.why: Prices inside images are unreadable on mobile, and a prepaid code shoppers only see in the cart can't help them decide.

changes.title: Engraving as one compact option
changes.what: Free engraving stays, as a single row with its limits: up to 9 characters, 50 and 100 ml, ships in 2–3 business days.
changes.why: A strong gift reason, but as a large box before the button it added a decision and pushed the button down.

changes.title: One primary button
changes.what: Add to cart is the only solid black button, with quantity inline. The maroon Buy now (UPI) becomes an outlined secondary.
changes.why: Each screen should have one primary action. Two heavy buttons in different colours split attention; express checkout stays without competing.

changes.title: Honest reassurance under the button
changes.what: Freshly made to order; a slot for dispatch time; the existing product-specialist chat as a link.
changes.why: With no returns, reassurance must come from craft and access to a person, not from a policy promise.

changes.title: A scent pyramid instead of note photos
changes.what: Five large note photos and the empty 'Scent Notes' accordion become a top / heart / base list from the product description, plus the main accords.
changes.why: The photos filled a screen before the button and listed different notes from the description. The pyramid answers what you'll smell, and when, at a glance.

changes.title: Accordions as the questions buyers ask
changes.what: How long does it last? When should I wear it? How do I apply it? What's in the bottle? Can I cancel or return it? Policy text kept in full.
changes.why: Question titles get more clicks than labels, and these match a first-time fragrance buyer's doubts.

changes.title: Sticky bar only after the inline button scrolls away
changes.what: Today the sticky add-to-cart bar shows from the first screen. Show it once the inline button has left the viewport.
changes.why: Asking for the sale before the page makes its case, with a duplicate button, adds noise to the first screen.

changes.title: Desktop: the buy box stays in view while the gallery scrolls
changes.what: Two columns: a seven-image gallery grid on the left, and a sticky buy box on the right carrying the full decision sequence.
changes.why: On desktop the gallery and the decision can sit side by side, so the button is always one glance away.

image_plan.why: Product first, in the mood the scent promises.

image_plan.show: A clean card: 'If you love Wanted by Night', listing the shared accords (warm spicy, cinnamon, woody) with small ingredient icons.
image_plan.overlay: If you love Wanted by Night
image_plan.why: Answers 'will it smell like it?' without showing the original brand's bottle.

image_plan.show: Today's infographic redesigned to be legible at phone size: 7h longevity, strong projection, best at night, seasons.
image_plan.why: Longevity is the second-biggest doubt; make it scannable.

image_plan.show: Raw materials arranged top to bottom: cinnamon and mandarin; cedar and incense; tobacco and leather.
image_plan.why: Turns notes into something the shopper can almost smell.

image_plan.show: 20, 50 and 100 ml bottles side by side, held in a hand.
image_plan.why: Shoppers can't judge ml; scale makes the 100 ml 'best value' tangible.

image_plan.show: A man spraying his collar before heading out, warm low light.
image_plan.why: Shows the occasion and the application tip in one frame.

image_plan.show: The box open with an engraved bottle; the engraving clearly legible.
image_plan.why: Sells the gift use and the free engraving.

image_plan.show: First-spray reaction; longevity check across a night; unboxing with engraving; a side-by-side scent test only if legal clears it.
image_plan.why: Video has the lowest drop-off and carries the 'real people like it' proof the page lacks.

summary.measurement: A/B test the new mobile page against the current one for 2–4 weeks if traffic allows; otherwise compare 3–4 weeks before and after, excluding the Diwali sale window. Primary metric: add-to-cart rate. Guard metrics: conversion rate and AOV (the 20 ml 'try first' nudge could lower AOV, so watch the size mix). Secondary: bundle share, engraving uptake, chat starts.

The brand's voice ('built to rule the night', 'beast mode')
Cancellation and refund terms, kept in full
Free engraving and the product-specialist chat
Maroon as the brand colour in the header, selection and savings
